facts.fact: Kannan is a goat-boy of about nine or ten; Chinna runs the kitchen door; Raiu is a young guard who holds the corridor torch outside the warden's chamber.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Neela to collect these three servant names at the feast.

facts.fact: Devan tells Neela the night guard layout: two on the west stair, four at the padippura, six on the wall in pairs, changing on the third clank after the middle watch.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Devan answering her questions with exact facts so she can map the chamber and fort.

facts.fact: Devan lays his sword on the floor on Neela's side of the bed, hilt toward her; the grip is plain wire, worn at the thumb.
facts.why: needed because the beat specifies the sword gesture.

facts.fact: Neela carries the guild's leopard tooth sewn into her waistband and the resin in a corked flask in a fold of her cloth.
facts.why: needed because the beat says she carries the tooth and uncorks the resin.

facts.fact: Devan says he took four months and asked twice to learn Raiu's name.
facts.why: needed to show contrast with Neela's habit and the shift in how he sees her.
